tasks.name: m4-force-push-range-diff
tasks.scopedGoal:
Land the force-push range-diff surface per PLAN.md §5.4 + §12 M4 + AUTONOMY_BRIEF.md §M4. When a PR's head_sha changes (force-push), the user can open a 'compared with previous push' view that shows old vs new commit ranges side-by-side with intra-line highlights. Prefer local `git range-diff` when a worktree is mapped to the PR (the M3 worktree mapping already exists); else fetch two head diffs via REST `/compare` and compute a Rust-side range-diff.

Deliverables:

1) Backend (Rust, `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/`):
   a) New module `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/range_diff/mod.rs` with:
      * `pub struct RangeDiff { pub old_range: CommitRange, pub new_range: CommitRange, pub commit_pairs: Vec<CommitPair>, pub mode: RangeDiffSource }` (RangeDiffSource = `LocalGit | RestCompare`).
      * `pub struct CommitRange { pub base_sha: String, pub head_sha: String, pub commits: Vec<CommitMetadata> }`.
      * `pub struct CommitPair { pub status: CommitPairStatus, pub old: Option<CommitMetadata>, pub new: Option<CommitMetadata>, pub intra_diff: Option<IntraDiff> }` where status is `Unchanged | Modified | Added | Removed` (matching `git range-diff` notation `=`, `!`, `+`, `-`).
      * `pub struct IntraDiff { pub hunks: Vec<IntraHunk> }` and `pub struct IntraHunk { pub old_lines: Vec<HighlightedLine>, pub new_lines: Vec<HighlightedLine> }` where `HighlightedLine { text: String, segments: Vec<HighlightSegment>, side: DiffSide }` and `HighlightSegment { start: usize, end: usize, kind: HighlightKind }` (HighlightKind = `Unchanged | Added | Removed`). All types `serde::Serialize + Deserialize + specta::Type`.
      * `pub trait RangeDiffSourceProvider { async fn compute(&self, account_id: &str, repo: &RepoLocator, base_sha: &str, old_head_sha: &str, new_head_sha: &str) -> Result<RangeDiff>; }` with two implementations:
        - `LocalGitRangeDiff { worktree_path: PathBuf }`: shells out to `git -C <worktree_path> range-diff --no-color --no-notes <base>...<old_head> <base>...<new_head>` (or use `git2` directly if the algorithm is feasible in-process; shelling out is acceptable and simpler — document the call in DECISIONS.md). Parses the `git range-diff` output into the `RangeDiff` struct above. Compute intra-line highlights via `similar` crate's `TextDiff::from_chars` (already a dep, or add it) on each modified pair's hunks. Robust against truncated worktrees: if the worktree doesn't have one of the commits, fall back to `git fetch origin <sha>` and retry once; if still missing, return `Err(WorktreeMissingCommits { missing_sha })` so the dispatcher can fall through to the REST path.
        - `RestCompareRangeDiff { github: Arc<GithubClient> }`: calls `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/compare/{base}...{old_head}` and `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/compare/{base}...{new_head}` (using the existing `octocrab`/`reqwest` client). Each response gives the commit list + file-level diffs. Pair commits by the SAME algorithm git uses (greedy by patch-id-equivalent — for v1, hash each commit's diff body with sha256 and pair on equal hashes; commits with no equal hash are added/removed; commits with similar but not equal patches are 'modified' based on jaccard similarity of file paths × line-count similarity). Reuse the intra-line highlight code from the LocalGit path.
      * `pub fn pick_provider(worktree: Option<WorktreeMapping>, github: Arc<GithubClient>) -> Box<dyn RangeDiffSourceProvider>`: prefers `LocalGitRangeDiff` when worktree is present AND high-confidence; else `RestCompareRangeDiff`.
   b) Migration `0011_push_history.sql` adding a `pr_pushes` table: `(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, pr_id TEXT NOT NULL, account_id TEXT NOT NULL, head_sha TEXT NOT NULL, base_sha TEXT NOT NULL, observed_at INTEGER NOT NULL, push_kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (push_kind IN ('initial', 'force-push', 'fast-forward', 'merge-back')), supersedes_head_sha TEXT, UNIQUE (pr_id, head_sha))`. The sync engine writes a row every time it observes a head_sha change on a PR via the PrDetail refetch loop. The `push_kind` is computed from the prior row + repo state (force-push when the new head doesn't have the old head as an ancestor; fast-forward when it does; merge-back when the old head is now in `base...new_head`). Add `0011_push_history.down.sql`. New read-model view `pr_force_push_pairs` exposes `(pr_id, base_sha, old_head_sha, new_head_sha, occurred_at)` tuples for the UI.
   c) IPC commands in `ipc/mod.rs`:
      * `list_pr_pushes(pr_id) -> Vec<PrPushView>` — return the push history for a PR.
      * `compute_range_diff(pr_id, base_sha, old_head_sha, new_head_sha) -> RangeDiff` — picks the provider via `range_diff::pick_provider` and returns the structured `RangeDiff`. Cached in-memory by `(pr_id, old_head_sha, new_head_sha)` for the session; recompute on force-push.
      All commands Specta-typed; regenerate `apps/desktop/src/lib/ipc/bindings.ts`.
   d) Rust integration tests under `apps/desktop/src-tauri/tests/`:
      * `range_diff_local_git.rs`: spin up a temp `git init` repo, create a base commit, two divergent head commits, force-push (simulated by overwriting the branch tip), and assert `LocalGitRangeDiff::compute(...)` returns the expected `RangeDiff` with the correct commit_pairs + intra-line highlights for a 3-line modification. Covers worktree-present path.
      * `range_diff_rest_compare.rs`: drive `RestCompareRangeDiff` against wiremock with canned `/compare` responses for both `<base>...<old_head>` and `<base>...<new_head>`. Assert the same RangeDiff shape as the local path on equivalent fixtures. Covers worktree-absent path.
      * `range_diff_fallback.rs`: configure `LocalGitRangeDiff` with a worktree that's missing one of the commits and `git fetch` is stubbed to fail. Assert it returns `Err(WorktreeMissingCommits)` and that `pick_provider` then falls through to the REST path under realistic conditions.

2) Frontend (Svelte 5, Primer CSS, `apps/desktop/src/`):

tasks.scopedGoal:
Land the M4 multi-account UI per PLAN.md §9 + §2.2 + §12 M4 + AUTONOMY_BRIEF.md §M4. M4 makes every viewer-dependent field account-scoped + lights up the multi-account aggregated inbox + adds composer posting identity + per-account rate-limit meter + foreground bypass demonstration.

1) Backend (Rust, `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/`):
   a) Refactor `RateLimitBudgeter` so the bucket state is keyed by `(account_id, ApiResource)`, not just `ApiResource`. Update `record` to pass account_id (already does); update `allow` to take `priority` + `account_id` so background calls for account A under low budget don't throttle account B's calls. Maintain backward compat where the call site still chooses the account. Foreground (`Priority::Foreground`) still bypasses throttling unconditionally per PLAN.md §2.2. Add a `pub fn snapshot(&self) -> Vec<(account_id, ApiResource, BudgetState)>` so the IPC layer can render the meter. Add a new `BudgetCommand::Snapshot` + `Allow { account_id, priority, reply_tx }` variant.
   b) Add migration `0012_multi_account_rate_limits.sql` extending the existing `rate_limit_buckets` table (created by M1) with `(used INTEGER, limit_total INTEGER)` columns IF not already present (it likely is — verify and add only if missing).    c) Aggregated inbox: the M1 inbox is per-account today (`db::list_inbox(account_id)`). Add a per-row `account_login` + `account_host` denormalization so the UI can render the badge without an extra IPC roundtrip. Add the IPC command `list_inbox(account_id_filter: Option<String>) -> Vec<InboxRow>` (or change the existing IPC signature; preserve backward compat by treating None as 'all accounts'). Specta-type the change; regenerate bindings.
   d) Foreground bypass observability: when `RateLimitBudgeter::allow` returns FALSE for a Background call, emit a `rate_limit_pressure:<account>` Tauri event with the current snapshot (so the UI can render 'throttled' state). When a Foreground call goes through under low budget, also emit `rate_limit_bypass:<account>` so the UI can show a brief 'foreground bypassed throttle' chip. Both events Specta-typed and surfaced via the existing emitter pattern.
   e) Composer posting identity: add an optional `posting_account_id` field to `SubmitPayload`. When set, the engine uses that account_id for the call to GitHub instead of the active session's account_id. Validate the account exists; reject otherwise. This matters for the multi-account composer where the user picks a different identity per submission.
   f) Rust integration tests:
      * `multi_account_rate_limit.rs`: simulate two accounts (A and B); set A's GraphQL remaining to 100 (below 1000 threshold), B's to 5000; call `allow(account_id='A', priority=Background)` → false; `allow(account_id='B', priority=Background)` → true; `allow(account_id='A', priority=Foreground)` → true (bypass). Assert a `rate_limit_pressure:A` event was emitted and a `rate_limit_bypass:A` event was emitted on the foreground call. Assert no events were emitted for B.
      * `multi_account_inbox.rs`: seed two accounts each with 5 PRs; assert `list_inbox(None)` returns 10 rows sorted by updated_at DESC with the correct account_login per row.
      * `composer_posting_identity.rs`: enqueue an AddComment with `posting_account_id='B'` while active session is A; assert the engine calls GitHub via account B's token (test via wiremock with two stubbed token validators).

2) Frontend (Svelte 5, Primer CSS, `apps/desktop/src/`):
   a) Account switcher polish (`apps/desktop/src/routes/+layout.svelte`):
      * Move the basic <select> into a dedicated `apps/desktop/src/lib/components/account/AccountSwitcher.svelte` Primer-styled dropdown (using `details-overlay` pattern) showing per-account login, host, and a small avatar (use `https://github.com/<login>.png` fallback). The dropdown has an 'All accounts' option that triggers the multi-account aggregated inbox.

The chip clicks navigate to the per-account inbox view as a convenience.

      * Extend `apps/desktop/src/lib/components/Composer.svelte`: above the textarea, render a Primer-styled posting-identity selector — a dropdown listing all accounts; default to the active account. When the user picks a different identity, the composer state's `postingAccountId` updates. On submit, that account_id is included in the `submit_mutation` IPC call (the IPC + engine support added in 1e above).
      * Add a Vitest test for the quick-switch flow.
   d) Per-account rate-limit meter (status bar):
      * Move the existing 'Rate limit' panel from `+layout.svelte`'s sidebar into a dedicated `apps/desktop/src/lib/components/status/RateLimitMeter.svelte` mounted in the status bar (footer or topbar). For the active account, render two rows: 'GraphQL: M/N points · resets in T' and 'REST: M/N · resets in T'. Use Primer Progress bars with color thresholds (green > 50%, yellow > 20%, red ≤ 20%). When `rate_limit_pressure:<account>` fires, the meter pulses red and shows a 'background throttled' chip. When `rate_limit_bypass:<account>` fires, the meter briefly shows a 'foreground bypassed throttle' chip with a `Counter` of bypass events in the last 30s.

Record a video or numbered screenshot sequence to `artifacts/m4-foreground-bypass/`.

tasks.scopedGoal:

Today the `auth` module supports a `host` field on accounts but the `api::GithubClient` defaults to `api.github.com` everywhere. GHE Server uses different base paths: `https://<ghe-host>/api/v3` for REST and `https://<ghe-host>/api/graphql` for GraphQL. This task wires per-host endpoint config end-to-end and proves the schema + auth flow doesn't break against a stubbed GHE host. NOT full feature parity — just enough that adding a GHE account + one InboxRefresh + one PrDetail round-trip succeed.

**STEP 0 (CHAIN INTEGRATION):** The cloud-agent branch was created from `orch/m4-merge-multiaccount/m4-multi-account`, so multi-account work is already present. Before doing anything else, integrate the other two M4 worker branches so this task can validate against the full M4 surface:

```
git fetch origin orch/m4-merge-multiaccount/m4-merge-surface orch/m4-merge-multiaccount/m4-force-push-range-diff
git merge --no-edit origin/orch/m4-merge-multiaccount/m4-merge-surface
git merge --no-edit origin/orch/m4-merge-multiaccount/m4-force-push-range-diff
```

Deliverables:

1) Backend (Rust, `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/`):
   a) Per-host endpoint config: extend `auth::AuthAccount` with `api_base_url` and `graphql_url` (derived from `host`):
      * For `host == "github.com"`: `api_base_url = https://api.github.com`, `graphql_url = https://api.github.com/graphql`.
      * For any other host (e.g. `ghe.example.com`): `api_base_url = https://<host>/api/v3`, `graphql_url = https://<host>/api/graphql`.
      * Optional override: an `EndpointOverride { api_base_url, graphql_url }` config readable from `~/.config/pr-cockpit/hosts.toml` (or platform-equivalent) keyed by host; if present, override the derived defaults. Useful for non-standard GHE deployments (e.g. behind a reverse proxy).
   b) Refactor `api::GithubClient` so every request uses the account's `api_base_url` / `graphql_url` from `AccountLocator` lookup, not a hardcoded `api.github.com`. The client should accept an `AccountResolver` (trait) that returns `(token, api_base_url, graphql_url)` for an account_id. Update all call sites in `mutations::handlers::*` and `sync::*` to pass the account_id correctly; they mostly already do. The change is internal — the public API surface (kept method signatures) should mostly survive.
   c) Auth flow per-host:
      * `auth::AuthService::switch_account` already exists. Extend it so the active host's endpoint config is loaded into the API client cache.
      * `auth::token_client::resolve_login_for_host(host, token)` already exists — verify it uses the right `api_base_url` per host (it should already, but confirm + add a test for `github.com` vs a stubbed GHE host).
      * Device flow and `gh` import: gate to `host == github.com` (GHE Server has separate device flow URLs we don't support yet; document the gap in DECISIONS.md). PAT import is the canonical GHE path. The 'Add account' UI shows the host field with `github.com` as default + a small 'GitHub Enterprise host?' link expanding the host input.
   d) Rust integration tests:
      * `ghe_endpoint_derivation.rs`: assert `api_base_url` / `graphql_url` derive correctly for `github.com` + `ghe.example.com` + a custom override from `hosts.toml`.
      * `ghe_round_trip.rs`: start a wiremock server at a custom port, register two AuthAccounts (one `github.com` pointing at `api.github.com`, one `ghe.local` pointing at the wiremock URL via override). Stub:
        - `POST https://ghe.local/api/graphql` returning the InboxRefresh response shape (one fixture PR).

        - `POST https://ghe.local/api/graphql` (PrDetail variant — dispatched by the operationName) returning the full PrDetail shape for the seeded PR.
        - `GET https://ghe.local/api/v3/repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}` (the REST head fetch the M3 sync still uses for some paths) returning a 200 with a minimal PR payload.
        Run the sync engine for the GHE account end-to-end; assert the SQLite state has the seeded PR rendered correctly. Assert no requests hit `api.github.com` for the GHE account.
      * `ghe_token_storage.rs`: assert a GHE token is stored in the keychain via `keyring` and is NEVER written to the SQLite `accounts` table or any log line. Reuses the existing token-leak test from M1 with the new host axis.

2) Frontend (Svelte 5, `apps/desktop/src/`):
   a) 'Add account' UI in `apps/desktop/src/routes/settings/`:
      * Find or create the settings → Accounts page. Add a small 'Add account' button that opens a modal asking for host (text input, default `github.com`) and token (password input) + a 'Validate + save' button.
